same_parameter_constraints: same phi, alpha, beta in original source and matched action library
same preparation, reference and complete record alphabet
deployment_quantifier: exists one policy from calibration and visible history, for all theta in the same allowed joint set

q_flag_calibration.coverage: conditional on fixed-q iid ideal flag sampling; inherited n=80000, radius=1/100, error<1/20
q_flag_calibration.design_optimality: entire [12/25,13/25] only, not every narrower realized confidence set

beta_pulse_assumption.origin: additional independent physical constraint; no measured beta calibration acquired
beta_pulse_assumption.flag_only_counterexample: beta=0 and beta=pi/2 give identical flags; from vacuum word01 has orthogonal terminal states and distance contribution Q01=156/625

full_record_contract.failure_reference_output: Tr_S[(Q tensor I) rho_SR (Q tensor I)] unnormalized, with S reset to g0
full_record_contract.conditional_target: normalized accepted extraction with derived H=s^2 I; original failures retain zero target mass but stay in source and cost
full_record_contract.finite_tester_scope: record-cell tests only unless terminal state/reference information supplies a separate valid CQ certificate

required_independent_certificates: actual low-spectral filter including failure reset and reference treatment
mean excitation budget for the actual joint input
source/library phi, alpha, beta matching or bounded full-output mismatch
blue-pulse area bound for omission and its applicable drift window
sideband effective-model validity, residual couplings and leakage
readout, preparation and terminal tester error model

error_budget.meaning: sufficient bound in the declared model, not a measured error or an empirical confidence interval

cost_contract.retry_formula: mu/(s_N*s^2) only for actually fresh/resettable independent source trials
cost_contract.calibration_amortization: C_cal/K per delivered output, separately from per-attempt mu
cost_contract.units: record resource vector with units and uncertainty before choosing a scalar conversion
